answer.body:
## A defect in the selected E009 criticism, not in the new construct

The defect I can establish is in the selected frozen E009 occurrence, and its effect is to make part of the vocabulary RSS inherited for “targets” carry a commitment the source text does not license. The new construct’s criticism-target talk then rests on that inherited vocabulary. I am not proposing to edit either; I am locating the defect and identifying the specific distinction it loses.

### The material on which the criticism depends

The new construct says:

> Under RSS's current resources, an account is a viewpoint, a reading, and a set of accepted conjectures. A criticism targets a specific element. P7's contribution is the observation that the *same sentence* (“this snapshot is inconsistent”) can target different elements.

and later:

> RSS already admits criticism of records, rules, coordinates, and assumptions as distinct elements; what I am adding is the indexing of a single criticism by its target, which RSS's current account structure does not explicitly perform…

RSS itself says:

> An account can be criticized by another account, and the criticism targets a specific element: a record, a rule, a booking history, a snapshot, a coordinate, or an assumption.

The selected E009 criticism, which is the frozen prior occurrence the construct is expressly built alongside, says of WHL:

> WHL’s `Conjecture` is `Snapshot → Prop`; `Refutation` is a snapshot plus a proof of negation. So every criticism is ultimately a criticism of a snapshot-level proposition. It cannot distinguish “the rule is bad” from “this record is corrupt” from “the assumption is false.” `Commitment := Prop` also loses account-relativity.

and later classifies the fix as a “Proposed repair: add `Account`, `Target`, and `Assumption` primitives. Not installed.”

### The defect

E009 asserts, as a defect of WHL, that WHL’s `Conjecture := Snapshot → Prop` makes “every criticism ultimately a criticism of a snapshot-level proposition,” and that recovering the rule/data/assumption distinction requires adding `Account`, `Target`, and `Assumption` primitives. That assertion passes a distinction from the frozen prose to a distinction between *types of conjecture*. The frozen prose draws the distinction between types of *thing criticized*, and it does so in a way that is not preserved by re-typing the conjecture as such:

> A criticism of the rule “higher revision always supersedes” is not the same as a criticism of a record that carries a high revision but an implausible quantity. Preserving that distinction matters because **one can reject a rule while accepting the data, or accept the rule while rejecting the data as corrupt or late.**

The decisive words are “reject a rule while accepting the data” and its converse. This is a claim about *permission to vary acceptance independently across the target types*. A criticism that rejects the rule and a criticism that rejects the record can be in force simultaneously without contradiction, and accepting the data does not by itself foreclose rejecting the rule. E009’s treatment — “every criticism is ultimately a criticism of a snapshot-level proposition” — collapses this into a single proposition whose refutation is a snapshot plus a negation. That is a different structure. A reader who builds on E009’s framing is invited to think the target taxonomy is discharged by adding a `Target` discriminant to each proposition, whereas the frozen prose’s point is that acceptance status itself is per target and can disagree across the targets in one account.

Note that RSS does not make this specific mistake. RSS says the criticism *targets a specific element*, and it does not say acceptance is proposition-global. So the defect is in E009, not in RSS. But the new construct says of itself that it “uses RSS's existing account/commitment/refutation vocabulary” and describes E009 as the standing prior occurrence of the packet; where the new construct claims to have simply carried RSS forward and where readers will read it alongside E009, the E009 framing is in the room. The construct’s own account of P7 (“the observation that the same sentence can target different elements”) inherits E009’s misreading of P7 as a claim about the proposition’s subject-matter rather than about the independence of acceptance.

### What is being questioned in P7’s sense

P7 distinguishes not only “which element is criticized” but “what it means to accept or reject each element.” Its example is explicit: rejecting the rule while accepting the data, or accepting the rule while rejecting the data. A criticism that treats “reject a rule while accepting the data” as one snapshot-level proposition that fails on some snapshots cannot model this, because the same snapshot is compatible with both acceptance and rejection of the rule depending on which other element of the same snapshot is taken as the target of acceptance. E009’s repaired vocabulary — `Account`, `Target`, `Assumption` — *could* express the distinction, but E009 does not say what it would take to express it, and its diagnosis at the point of the defect implies the distinction is unavailable without those primitives, which would make it unavailable in RSS too if RSS were read the same way.

### What is established versus proposed

Established by the available evidence: E009 says “every criticism is ultimately a criticism of a snapshot-level proposition” and proposes adding `Target` and related primitives as the repair. The frozen P7 says preservation of the target distinction “matters because one can reject a rule while accepting the data, or accept the rule while rejecting the data.” These two passages are not equivalent, and reading E009’s sentence as a characterization of the P7 distinction loses the specific per-target independence of acceptance. This is a substantive (if localized) defect in E009’s characterization, not merely a stylistic restatement.

Proposed rather than established: that the new construct’s “target-conditional criticism” depends on this at the point where it says “RSS already admits criticism of records, rules, coordinates, and assumptions as distinct elements.” RSS may admit the distinction without inheriting E009’s mischaracterization. My point is narrower: the construct’s “uses RSS’s existing account/commitment/refutation vocabulary” claim is in tension with the E009 occurrence it is packaged with, and a reader who takes both literally has no account of *why* per-target acceptance independence is preserved rather than presupposed.

### A rival reading that must remain open

E009 could be read charitably as speaking about the *only* mechanism WHL has for stating a conjecture, not about the target taxonomy as such. So long as the target taxonomy is not being claimed to reduce to snapshot-indexed propositions, the two passages can coexist as “WHL is limited in how it can state things” and “P7 distinguishes target types.” On that charitable reading, there is no defect in E009, only a compression of its scope. I cannot rule this reading out from the excerpt alone; the sentence “So every criticism is ultimately a criticism of a snapshot-level proposition” reads more strongly than the charitable reading permits, but the “So” may be doing local inferential work about WHL rather than a universal claim about criticism in general. Since this is not decidable from the excerpt, I retain the rival account rather than treat the defect as fully established.

### What I am not claiming

I am not claiming RSS is incomplete here, nor that the new construct should be modified, nor that “target-conditional criticism” fails its own stated purpose. I am not claiming the P7 distinction is missing from RSS’s primitive list. I am not installing any repair in E009 or RSS. And I am not proposing to replace the frozen construct. The only thing established is that E009’s sentence about “every criticism is ultimately a criticism of a snapshot-level proposition” does not, without further argument, preserve the frozen P7 claim about per-target independence of acceptance, and the new construct does not provide that further argument when it says it “uses RSS's existing account/commitment/refutation vocabulary” alongside E009.
